A head is twice as likely as a tail, so $P(H) = 2P(T)$. The probabilities sum to 1.
$$\begin{aligned} P(H) + P(T) &= 1 \\ 2P(T) + P(T) &= 1 \\ P(T) &= \dfrac{1}{3} \end{aligned}$$

The formula is $S = V_0 \times (0.80)^n$, so each year the value is $80\%$ of the previous value.

$$\begin{aligned} \text{Annual depreciation} &= 12.2\% \times 50\,000 \\ &= \$6100 \end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned} 25\,600 &= 50\,000 - 6100n \\ -24\,400 &= -6100n \\ n &= \dfrac{-24\,400}{-6100} \\ &= 4 \end{aligned}$$

Interest is 6% per annum compounded monthly, so the rate per month is $r=\dfrac{0.06}{12}=0.005$ and the number of periods is $n=12$.
$$\begin{aligned} FV &= 35\,000(1+0.005)^{12} \\ &= 35\,000(1.005)^{12} \\ &\approx \$37\,158.72 \end{aligned}$$

Suppose a new value, $x$, is added to this dataset, giving the following.

$$1 \quad 5 \quad 9 \quad 10 \quad 15 \quad x$$

It is known that $x$ is greater than 15. It is also known that the difference between the means of the two datasets is equal to ten times the difference between the medians of the two datasets.

Calculate the value of $x$.

solutions.latex:
For the first dataset:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{mean} &= \dfrac{1+5+9+10+15}{5} = 8 \\ \text{median} &= 9 \end{aligned}$$
For the second dataset, since $x>15$ it is the largest value:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{mean} &= \dfrac{40+x}{6} \\ \text{median} &= \dfrac{9+10}{2} = 9.5 \end{aligned}$$
The difference in means equals ten times the difference in medians:
$$\begin{aligned} \dfrac{40+x}{6}-8 &= 10(9.5-9) \\ \dfrac{40+x}{6}-8 &= 5 \\ \dfrac{40+x}{6} &= 13 \\ 40+x &= 78 \\ x &= 38 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ x = 38$$
criteria: Calculates the mean and median of the first dataset and the mean of the second dataset, or equivalent merit

4509.stem:
Mr Ali, Ms Brown and a group of students were camping at the site located at $P$. Mr Ali walked with some of the students on a bearing of $035^\circ$ for 7 km to location $A$. Ms Brown, with the rest of the students, walked on a bearing of $100^\circ$ for 9 km to location $B$.

solutions.latex:
North lines at $P$ give the bearings measured clockwise from north.
$$\begin{aligned} \angle APB &= 100^\circ-35^\circ \\ &= 65^\circ \end{aligned}$$

Using the cosine rule in $\triangle APB$:
$$\begin{aligned} AB^2 &= 7^2+9^2-2\times 7\times 9\cos 65^\circ \\ &= 76.75\ldots \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ AB \approx 8.76 \text{ km}$$
criteria: Attempts to use the cosine rule to find the distance $AB$

solutions.latex:
Using the sine rule in $\triangle APB$ to find $\angle PAB$:
$$\dfrac{\sin A}{9} = \dfrac{\sin 65^\circ}{8.76\ldots}$$
$$A = 68.6\ldots^\circ \approx 69^\circ$$
The bearing of $B$ from $A$ is found using the angle at $A$ and the north line at $A$:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Bearing} &= 180^\circ-(69^\circ-35^\circ) \\ &= 146^\circ \end{aligned}$$

$$AB = 80\div 10 = 8 \text{ cm}$$

$$\angle AOB = 360^\circ\div 10 = 36^\circ$$
Triangle $OAB$ is isosceles ($OA=OB=r$), so
$$\angle OAB = \dfrac{180^\circ-36^\circ}{2} = 72^\circ$$
Using the sine rule in $\triangle OAB$:
$$\dfrac{r}{\sin 72^\circ} = \dfrac{8}{\sin 36^\circ}$$
$$r = 12.944\ldots$$
The area is ten times the area of $\triangle OAB$:
$$\begin{aligned} A &= 10\times\dfrac{1}{2}\times(12.944\ldots)^2\times\sin 36^\circ \\ &\approx 492.4 \text{ cm}^2 \end{aligned}$$

4513.stem:
The Intelligence Quotient (IQ) scores for adults in City $A$ are normally distributed with a mean of 108 and a standard deviation of 10.

The IQ scores for adults in City $B$ are normally distributed with a mean of 112 and a standard deviation of 16.

parts.latex:
Yin is an adult who lives in City $A$ and has an IQ score of 128.

What percentage of the adults in this city have an IQ score higher than Yin's?

There are 1 000 000 adults living in City $B$.

Calculate the number of adults in City $B$ that would be expected to have an IQ score lower than Yin's.

Simon, an adult who lives in City $A$, moves to City $B$. The $z$-score corresponding to his IQ score in City $A$ is the same as the $z$-score corresponding to his IQ score in City $B$.

By first forming an equation, calculate Simon's IQ score. Give your answer correct to one decimal place.

solutions.latex:
$$\dfrac{128-108}{10} = 2$$
So $128$ is 2 standard deviations above the mean.

About $95\%$ of scores lie within 2 standard deviations, so $5\%$ lie outside, split equally between the two tails.
$$\therefore\ \dfrac{5\%}{2} = 2.5\% \text{ have an IQ score higher than Yin's}$$
criteria: Demonstrates that $97.5\%$ relates to 2 standard deviations above the mean, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
Mean of City $B$ is $112$, so one standard deviation above the mean is
$$112+16 = 128$$
So Yin's score is 1 standard deviation above the mean in City $B$.

The percentage with a lower score is
$$50\%+\dfrac{1}{2}\times 68\% = 84\%$$
The expected number of adults is
$$1\,000\,000\times 0.84 = 840\,000$$
criteria: Demonstrates Yin is 1 standard deviation above the mean in City $B$, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
Let $x$ be Simon's IQ score. Using $z=\dfrac{x-\mu}{\sigma}$:
$$\begin{aligned} z_A &= \dfrac{x-108}{10} \\ z_B &= \dfrac{x-112}{16} \end{aligned}$$
The $z$-scores are equal:
$$\begin{aligned} \dfrac{x-108}{10} &= \dfrac{x-112}{16} \\ 16(x-108) &= 10(x-112) \\ 16x-1728 &= 10x-1120 \\ 6x &= 608 \\ x &\approx 101.3 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{Simon's IQ score is } 101.3$$
criteria: Provides correct equation linking City $A$ with City $B$

A scientist wants to explore the relationship between the temperature in degrees Celsius and the number of cricket chirps heard in a 15-second time interval.

\item The mean temperature in the dataset is $0.525^\circ\text{C}$ below the median temperature in the dataset.
\item A total of 684 chirps was counted when collecting the 20 data points.
\end{itemize}

The scientist fits a least-squares regression line using the data $(x, y)$, where $x$ is the temperature in degrees Celsius and $y$ is the number of chirps heard in a 15-second time interval. The equation of this line is

$$y = -10.6063 + bx,$$

where $b$ is the slope of the regression line.

The least-squares regression line passes through the point $(\bar{x}, \bar{y})$ where $\bar{x}$ is the sample mean of the temperature data and $\bar{y}$ is the sample mean of the chirp data.

Calculate the number of chirps expected in a 15-second interval when the temperature is $19^\circ$ Celsius. Give your answer correct to the nearest whole number.

solutions.latex:
The median temperature is $22$, read from the box-plot, so
$$\bar{x} = 22-0.525 = 21.475$$
$$\bar{y} = \dfrac{684}{20} = 34.2$$
The regression line passes through $(\bar{x},\bar{y})$:
$$\begin{aligned} 34.2 &= -10.6063+b(21.475) \\ b &= \dfrac{44.8063}{21.475} \\ &= 2.08644\ldots \end{aligned}$$
When $x=19$:
$$\begin{aligned} y &= -10.6063+2.08644\ldots\times 19 \\ &= 29.03606\ldots \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ 29 \text{ chirps are expected}$$
criteria: Finds value of $b$, or equivalent merit

The value, $V$, of the machine after $n$ years is given by the formula

$$V = 60000 \times 0.85^{n}$$

parts.latex: By what percentage rate will the machine depreciate annually?
Calculate the value of the machine after three years.
At the end of which year will the machine’s value first fall below $\$12\,000$?

The formula $V = 60000\times 0.85^n$ has $1 - 0.15 = 0.85$ as its multiplier.

Substitute $n=3$.
$$\begin{aligned} V &= 60000\times 0.85^3 \\ &= \$36\,847.50 \end{aligned}$$

Test values of $n$ in $V = 60000\times 0.85^n$.
$$\begin{aligned} n=8:\ V &= 60000\times 0.85^8 = \$16\,349.43 \\ n=10:\ V &= 60000\times 0.85^{10} = \$11\,812.46 \end{aligned}$$

The monthly rate and number of repayments are
$$r = 6\%\div 12 = 0.5\% ,\qquad n = 25\times 12 = 300$$
From the table, the interest factor is $155.2069$, so
$$\begin{aligned} R &= 450\,000\div 155.2069 \\ &= \$2899.36 \end{aligned}$$

The loan has reduced by
$$450\,000 - 448\,698.03 = \$1301.97$$
The total repayments are
$$2\times 2899.36 = \$5798.72$$
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Interest} &= 5798.72 - 1301.97 \\ &= \$4496.75 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Finds the loan reduction, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
A spanning tree on $n$ vertices has $n-1$ edges. There are $8$ cities.
$$\begin{aligned} n-1 &= 8-1 \\ &= 7 \text{ edges} \end{aligned}$$

Choosing the cheapest edges that join all cities without forming a cycle gives the minimum spanning tree.

The edges are Almaty–Chennai $330$, Almaty–Yerevan $485$, Yerevan–Bishkek $450$, Bishkek–Kabul $275$, Kabul–Dili $370$, Bishkek–Xi'an $445$, Xi'an–Seoul $620$.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Length} &= 330 + 485 + 450 + 370 + 275 + 445 + 620 \\ &= 2975 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{length of minimum spanning tree} = \$2975$$
criteria: Draws a correct tree or finds the correct length, or equivalent merit

Calculate the distance $DF$ and hence find the angle of the seating, $\alpha$, to the nearest degree.

solutions.latex:
Since $\angle ABD$ and the $51^\circ$ elevation angle lie on a straight line, they are supplementary.
$$\angle ABD = 180^\circ - 51^\circ = 129^\circ$$
In $\triangle ABD$, the angle at $A$ is $28^\circ$. By the angle sum of a triangle:
$$\begin{aligned} \angle ADB + 28^\circ + 129^\circ &= 180^\circ \\ \angle ADB &= 23^\circ \end{aligned}$$

meta.format_note: A solution diagram would help but the question's figure is used.

solutions.latex:
Use the sine rule in $\triangle ABD$.
$$\dfrac{BD}{\sin 28^\circ} = \dfrac{44}{\sin 23^\circ}$$
$$\begin{aligned} BD &= \dfrac{44\sin 28^\circ}{\sin 23^\circ} \\ &\approx 53 \text{ m} \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Writes the correct sine rule equation, or equivalent merit

meta.format_note: Rubric written by us.

solutions.latex:
In right-angled $\triangle BCD$, with $BD = 53$ and angle $51^\circ$ at $B$:
$$\sin 51^\circ = \dfrac{DC}{53}$$
$$\begin{aligned} DC &= 53\sin 51^\circ \\ &\approx 41.19 \text{ m} \end{aligned}$$
The seating begins $4$ m above ground, so
$$DF = DC - 4 = 53\sin 51^\circ - 4$$
Also
$$\cos 51^\circ = \dfrac{BC}{53}$$
$$BC = 53\cos 51^\circ$$
The seating angle satisfies
$$\tan\alpha = \dfrac{53\sin 51^\circ - 4}{53\cos 51^\circ}$$
$$\therefore\ \alpha \approx 48^\circ$$

Scarlett lives with her parents and two siblings. Every evening her parents watch television together for 2.5 hours and Scarlett and her siblings are on their devices for 4 hours.

If the average rate for electricity is \$0.17/kWh and the household receives a 25% discount for paying all of their bills on time, how much does it cost to run the television and children's devices each year?

solutions.latex:
Energy is power times time. Find the Wh used in a week (7 evenings).

Television (one set, 2.5 hours):
$$\text{TV} = 270\times 7\times 2.5 = 4725 \text{ Wh}$$
Devices (3 children, 4 hours):
$$\text{Devices} = 3\times 130\times 7\times 4 = 10\,920 \text{ Wh}$$
Convert to kilowatt-hours by dividing by $1000$.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Total} &= \dfrac{4725 + 10\,920}{1000} \\ &= 15.645 \text{ kWh} \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ 15.645 \text{ kWh per week}$$
criteria: Finds the weekly consumption of both the television and the devices, or equivalent merit
Finds the weekly consumption of the television or the devices, or equivalent merit

meta.format_note: Rubric written by us.

solutions.latex:
There are 52 weeks in a year.
$$\text{Electricity per year} = 15.645\times 52 = 813.54 \text{ kWh}$$
The 25% discount means paying $75\%$ of the cost.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Cost} &= 813.54\times 0.17\times 0.75 \\ &= \$103.73 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{Cost} = \$103.73 \text{ per year}$$

Adele decides to make a larger batch while maintaining the recipe's proportions. She uses 15 more oranges than lemons.

parts.latex: Determine the number of oranges Adele will need for this larger batch.
Using this information, calculate the total amount of sugar required for Adele's batch of marmalade.

solutions.latex:
Let $O$ be the number of oranges and $L$ the number of lemons. The recipe ratio gives $\dfrac{O}{L} = \dfrac{5}{2}$, and $O = L + 15$.
$$\dfrac{L+15}{L} = \dfrac{5}{2}$$
$$\begin{aligned} 2L + 30 &= 5L \\ 3L &= 30 \\ L &= 10 \end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} O &= 10 + 15 \\ &= 25 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ 25 \text{ oranges}$$

meta.format_note: Rubric written by us.

Sugar is in proportion to oranges.
$$\dfrac{800}{5} = 160 \text{ g of sugar per orange}$$
$$\begin{aligned} 25\times 160 &= 4000 \text{ g} \\ &= 4 \text{ kg} \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ 4 \text{ kg of sugar}$$

parts.latex: Use the trapezoidal rule with a single application to estimate the area of the irregular region.

Initially, the ocean pool is filled with a mixture of fresh water and chlorinated water in the ratio 7:18. After some water is removed, 1000 kL remains. To refill the pool, 100 kL of fresh water is added first, and the remaining volume is restored to 1900 kL using chlorinated water.

Determine the new ratio of fresh water to chlorinated water after the refill.

solutions.latex:
Apply the trapezoidal rule with one application, $A \approx \dfrac{h}{2}(d_f + d_l)$, with $h = 40$ m and the two end measurements $30$ m and $10$ m.
$$\begin{aligned} A &\approx \dfrac{40}{2}(30 + 10) \\ &= 800 \text{ m}^2 \end{aligned}$$

meta.format_note: Rubric written by us. Values 40, 30, 10 taken from source (figure not viewed).

solutions.latex:
The volume is the total area times the depth of $2$ m.
$$\begin{aligned} V &= (\text{semicircle} + \text{irregular region})\times \text{depth} \\ &= \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\times \pi\times 10^2 + 800\right)\times 2 \\ &= 1914.16\ldots \text{ m}^3 \\ &\approx 1900 \text{ m}^3 \end{aligned}$$
Since $1 \text{ m}^3 = 1 \text{ kL}$, the capacity is $1900$ kL to 2 significant figures.
criteria: Finds the total area or the volume, or equivalent merit

meta.format_note: Rubric written by us.

solutions.latex:
The ratio $7:18$ has $25$ parts. Scale it to $1000$ kL.
$$7:18 = 280:720$$
After the refill the total is $1900$ kL. Fresh water is $280 + 100$ and chlorinated water is the rest.
$$\text{fresh} = 280 + 100 = 380 \text{ kL}$$
$$\text{chlorinated} = 1900 - 380 = 1520 \text{ kL}$$
$$380 : 1520 = 1 : 4$$
$$\therefore\ \text{New ratio} = 1:4$$
